originality.rationale: The new result supplies the explicit joint Poisson void exponent for two extremal chords sharing one endpoint and a fixed-angle triangular-array near-tie crossover. Lao 2010 Theorem 6.8 assumes disjoint diameter endpoint neighborhoods of regular even-gons; its odd-polygon result samples edges rather than interior. Appel et al. (2002) work under a unique major axis per Lao 2010 and Schrempp 2015, which fails at exact side tie. Schrempp 2015 explicitly assumes one axis and curved endpoints; Mayer–Molchanov 2006 consider balls. Actual semantic published-record comparisons found no dominating claim; their closest entries concern short-distance laws or boundary-based extremes. A plausible 2002 original was unavailable in full and remains a priority risk; this was not represented as fully inspected or as automatic proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The original Appel–Najim–Russo 2002 article was inaccessible in full; its unique-axis restriction was corroborated indirectly, but hidden appendices or variants cannot be excluded.
Literature not indexed by searched mathematical descriptions might contain the same shared-endpoint limit or crossover.
The theorem is a narrow but mathematically motivated fixed-angle triangular-array result; no general polygon theorem is proved.
